title: Isolation and comparison of neural stem cells from the adult rat brain and spinal cord canonical neurogenic niches
protocol: Euthanize the animal by inducing deep anesthesia with 4% Isoflurane followed by decapitation.
Disinfect the animal thoroughly before starting the dissection.
Remove the head from the body.
Cut open the scalp to expose the skull using surgical scissors.
Cut off the remnant of the spinal column with bone scissors.
Break open the back of the skull with rongeurs.
Cut away the pieces of skull with bone scissors.
Insert the sharp blade of the surgical scissors into the skull along the longitudinal fissure and cut open the skull.
Remove the surgical scissors and carefully insert the Heidemann spatula through the crack down the midline.
Release the Dura Mater from the skull on both sides before opening the skull with the rongeurs.
Extract the brain with a curved hippocampal dissection tool when fully exposed.
Transfer the extracted brain to an ice-cold glass plate and soak in ice-cold sterile saline.
Discard remains and surgical barrier sheet.
Remove the remaining part of the brain stem, cerebellum, and largest part of the basal ganglia, exposing the hippocampus on one hemisphere.
Cut the hippocampus in two equal parts down the middle along the Dorsal-Ventral axis.
Extract the dorsal hippocampal section.
Locate the dentate gyrus within the hippocampal formation.
Extract the dentate gyrus from the hippocampal formation.
Remove the dentate gyrus after extraction from the hippocampal formation.
Periodically douse the tissue in ice-cold sterile saline.
Remove the cerebellum entirely before separating the two hemispheres sagittally down the midline using a sterilized and chilled razor blade.
Remove the remaining part of the brain stem, cerebellum, and as much of the basal ganglia as possible with bone scissors to expose the hippocampus on one hemisphere.
Cut the hippocampus in two equal parts down the middle (dorsal-ventral) using the Heidemann spatula.
Gently move the Heidemann spatula underneath the dorsal hippocampal section and gently flip it out of the brain onto a filter paper-covered chilled glass plate.
Isolate the dentate gyrus from the rest of the hippocampal formation using the Heidemann spatula and forceps.
Dice the dentate gyrus tissue thoroughly with a chilled and sterile razor blade.
Transfer diced dentate gyrus tissue to a vial containing ice-cold Neurobasal 1× using a graduated transfer pipette.
Repeat for the second hemisphere.
Transport tissue from both hemispheres in the same 15 ml tube on ice.
Remove the cerebellum entirely from the brain before separating the two hemispheres sagittally down the midline using a sterilized and chilled razor blade.
Cut one hemisphere coronally 0.5 mm anterior to the hippocampal apex, using the apical tip of the hippocampus as a marker.
Discard the caudal part of the brain hemisphere after cutting.
Trim away remnants of basal ganglia from the cut hemisphere using fine forceps and small dissection scissors.
Cut away overhanging cortex to fully expose the Subventricular zone.
Ensure tissue remains chilled at all times by periodically dousing it in ice-cold sterile saline.
Using Vannas spring scissors and forceps, gently cut out the anterior 2/3 of the lateral SVZ in a single thin sheet.
Ensure the tissue excised is uniformly light brown.
Transfer the dissected SVZ onto filter paper-covered chilled glass plate.
Dice the SVZ thoroughly with a sterile and chilled razor blade.
Transfer diced SVZ to a vial containing ice-cold Neurobasal 1× using a graduated transfer pipette.
Repeat dissection for the second hemisphere.
Combine tissue from both hemispheres in the same 15 mL tube on ice.
Open up chest and stomach, removing all internal organs using surgical scissors.
Cut through the spinal column at the base of the animal’s neck using bone scissors.
Release the skin of the back from the spinal column and ribs down to the hips.
Cut through the spinal column just rostral to the Rectus Femoris muscles using bone scissors.
Insert one blade of the dissection scissors into the spinal column.
Carefully cut both sides of each vertebra to expose the spinal cord.
Cut 1 vertebra at a time, always pointing the tip of the dissection scissors outwards, away from the spinal cord.
Quickly douse the exposed spinal cord with ice-cold sterile saline before extraction.
Grip the rostral tip of the spinal cord with a pair of fine forceps (non-dominant hand).
Lift gently until resistance is met.
Carefully cut the root ganglia on either side stepwise with a pair of small dissection scissors (dominant hand) while gently lifting the spinal cord as it releases.
Cut the spinal cord right below the lumbar enlargement.
Transfer the spinal cord to the filter paper-covered chilled glass plate and douse again with ice-cold sterile saline.
Cut the spinal cord into 2–3 1 cm long pieces using a chilled and sterile razor blade.
Gently cut off the white matter on either side of the piece of spinal cord (lateral sides).
Cut the white matter off the top of the spinal cord.
Grab the gray matter containing the central canal with fine forceps.
Carefully cut it off from the remaining ventral white matter of the spinal cord piece.
Remove filter paper and place the piece of gray matter onto a clean part of the glass plate.
Dice thoroughly with a sterile and chilled razor blade.
Transfer to the vial with ice-cold Neurobasal 1× using a graduated transfer pipette for transport and dissociation.
Repeat the procedure for the remaining spinal cord sections, starting with 1–2 and expanding to 2–3 when more experienced.
Clean the extracted tissue off white matter during dissection.
Transport tissue from all sections in the same 15 mL tube on ice.
Spin down the tissue at 100 × g for 1 minute at room temperature.
Aspirate the transport media and resuspend the tissue in 5 mL ice-cold HBSS −/− using a serological pipette.
Spin down the tissue at 100 × g for 1 minute at room temperature.
Repeat steps of aspirating and resuspending the tissue once.

Aspirate the HBSS and resuspend the tissue from one animal in 1 mL accutase for dissociating CC- or SVZ-derived tissue, or in 1 mL trypsin for dissociating SGZ-derived tissue, ensuring the solution is at least at room temperature when added.
Incubate the tissue for 15 min in an incubator at 37°C using accutase or 5 min using trypsin.
Mechanically dissociate the tissue by repeatedly triturating the solution 500 times using a p100 or p200 pipette set to 100 μL.
Avoid introducing bubbles during pipetting steps.
Hold the shaft of the pipette at the opening of the 15 mL tube while aspirating.
Transfer the dissociated tissue into a new 15 mL tube containing 1 mL warm wash media.
Wash the lower part of the inside of the original tube using 1 mL warm Neurobasal 1× wash media.
Add the washed solution to a new tube.
Add another 2 mL of Neurobasal 1× wash media to achieve a final volume of 5 mL.
Spin down the cells at 150 × g for 5 min at room temperature (20°C–23°C).
Aspirate the washing media.
Resuspend the pellet in 4 mL warm wash media.
Spin down the cells again at 150 × g for 5 min at room temperature (20°C–23°C).
Repeat steps of washing and resuspending the cell pellet once more.
Prepare a non-tissue culture-treated 6-well plate by adding 3.5 mL of culturing media to 1-3 wells during wash steps.
Place the prepared plate in a humidified incubator (5% CO2, 37°C).
Remove the wash media after the second wash.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL culturing media.
Take 10 μL of resuspended cell solution and add it to 10 μL of 0.4% Trypan Blue in a 500 μL Eppendorf.
Mix gently but thoroughly by triturating 10× times.
Apply 10 μL to both sides of a cell counting chamber slide.
Count the cells using an automatic cell counter (or other method of choice).
Record the numbers from both sides of the chip.

Determine the volume containing 5 × 10^5 live cells by calculating: Average of total number of live cells ÷ 1000 for number of live cells per μL of cell solution. Then, 5 × 10^5 ÷ number of live cells/μL gives how many μL of cell suspension contain 5 × 10^5 live cells.
Add the volume of cell suspension containing 5 × 10^5 live cells to each well in the 6-well plate prepared previously.
Place the plate in a humidified incubator (5% CO2, 37°C) and leave undisturbed for 4 days.
Ensure P0 NSCs form adherent cultures on the well bottom.
After P1 passage, ensure all NSCs form an adherent monolayer prior to the first media change.
Seed NSCs on glass coverslips coated with Poly-L-Ornithine and Laminin solution for optimal survival and proliferation.
Provide a rough physical environment for SGZ-derived NSC monolayer cultures to thrive.
Leave the cells in the incubator for 4 days to expand following dissociation before the first media change.
Prepare media according to specified tables and pre-warm to 37°C in a water bath.
Remove cell media from one well using a 5 mL serological pipette, tritrate 2–3 times to wash off any adherent cells.
Transfer the media to an empty 15 mL tube.
Triturate cell-containing media quickly 3–4 times to clean the neurospheres of any adherent cell debris.
Pipette 1 mL of fresh media into the well using the same pipette, making sure any remaining cells are submerged.
Repeat the procedure for remaining wells on the same plate.
Centrifuge the tube containing the cells at 150 × g for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Remove supernatant from the centrifuged cells.
Replace with 2 mL fresh media per well.
Using a p1000 pipette, triturate 3–4 times to break up the pellet and return cells to their wells.
Triturate twice before reseeding each well to maintain an equal number of cells between the wells.
Pool and count all wells seeded from the same initial population as one experimental unit for accurate cell counts and rate of proliferation records.
Harvest cells on day 0, change media on days 4 and 7, passage to P1 on day 10.
Change media on days 13, 16, and 18, passage to P2 on day 20 for subsequent generations.
Monitor media acidification (phenol red shifting to a yellow hue) and adjust media change frequency as needed based on growth rate.
Remove media with cells using a 5 mL serological pipette and transfer to an empty 15 mL tube.
Add 1 mL warm (37°C) Neurobasal 1× to the well to keep attached cells hydrated, ensuring not to dislodge any adherent cells.
Centrifuge the tube containing cells at 150 × g for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend cells in dissociation agent (accutase/trypsin) at a ratio of 1 mL per well.
Carefully remove the hydration media from each well, ensuring not to detach any adherent cells.
Triturate the dissociation agent with cells twice, aspirate, and return 1 mL to each well.
Incubate cells for 15 minutes (accutase) or 5 minutes (trypsin) in an incubator at 5% CO2 and 37°C.
Aspirate off the dissociation agent following incubation.
Use the dissociation agent to wash the bottom of the well, collecting all cells in a 15 mL tube.
Mechanically dissociate the cells by trituration using a p200 pipette for volumes ≤ 2 mL or a p1000 pipette for volumes > 2 mL, approximately 20% of the total volume at a time.
Mix 4 mL of warm Neurobasal 1× wash media with the tube containing the dissociation agent.
Spin down the cells at 150 × g for 5 min at room temperature (20°C–23°C).
Aspirate off the washing media and resuspend the pellet in 4 mL warm wash media using a p1000 pipette set to 1000 μL.
Spin down the cells again at 150 × g for 5 min at room temperature (20°C–23°C).
Repeat the washing step once more.
Prepare 6-well culture plates by adding 3 mL of culturing media.
Place the prepared plates in a humidified incubator (5% CO2, 37°C).
Remove wash media after the second wash step.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of culturing media.
Take 10 μL of resuspended cell solution and add to 10 μL of 0.4% Trypan Blue.
Mix gently but thoroughly (about 10 aspirations) in an Eppendorf tube.
Apply 10 μL to both sides of a cell counting chamber slide.
Count the cells using an automatic cell counter or other method of choice.
Record numbers from both sides of the chip.
Double the number of wells on each passage for adequate space expansion.
Split the cell solution evenly between new wells.
Return the plate with new wells to the humidified incubator (5% CO2, 37°C).
Gently swirl the plate in clockwise and counterclockwise directions to ensure even distribution.
Label cells using EdU at a 1:500 dilution in cell media.
Replace 50% of the cell media with EdU solution to achieve a final concentration of 1:1000 (10 μM/mL) per well.
Incubate cells in EdU solution for 12–24 hours as desired.
Fix cells by submerging them in 3% glyoxal solution for 15 minutes (300 μL/well in 24-well plates, adjust volume accordingly).
Remove the glyoxal solution and wash cells twice with 1× PBS for 5 minutes each, increasing the PBS volume by 100 μL per wash.
Remove PBS from wash and replace with 0.5% Triton-X 100 in 1× PBS for 5 min.
Remove Triton-X and wash twice for 5 min with 1× PBS, increasing volume of PBS for each wash.
Replace PBS with 5% Goat Serum diluted in 1× PBS (blocking solution) and set aside for 1 h (300 μL/well is enough for 24 well plates).
Prepare primary antibody solution in 5% goat serum at this time and store in fridge until needed.
Remove goat serum blocking solution and submerge cells with primary antibody solution.
Transfer plates into the cold room and place onto shaker table and leave overnight (18–22 h, at 4°C).
Always leave 1 well without primary antibodies for a primary antibody exclusion control.
Prepare secondary antibodies (1:500 standard solution) in 5% goat serum in 1× PBS.
Centrifuge secondary antibody solution at 2,000 × g for approx. 15 min.
Remove primary antibody solution.
Wash with 1× PBS three times for 5 minutes each, increasing the volume of PBS for each wash.
Submerge cells in the secondary solution after removing PBS.
Place on a shaker table set to low speed and leave for 3 hours, protected from light.
Warm Prolong Gold Antifade mounting media at room temperature.
Prepare Hoechst solution (1:2000) in 1× PBS and protect from light during the last 30 minutes of secondary incubation time.
Remove secondary solution and submerge cells in the Hoechst solution for 30 minutes (300 μL/well).
Wash with 1× PBS three times, increasing the volume of PBS for each wash after removing Hoechst solution.
Wash once with MQ water.
Replace MQ water with new MQ water (700 μL/well for a 24 well plate).
Prepare cover slide and mark with date, sample type, and secondary antibody wavelength.
Add a small drop of mounting media onto the cover slide.
Remove coverslip from the well with fine forceps and dry by gently tapping one edge onto a sheet of tissue paper.
Mount the coverslip by touching the mounting media with one side of the coverslip, then slowly lowering the other side, ensuring that no air bubbles are trapped under it.
Check the mounted coverslip with a fluorescent microscope at low magnification for DAPI/Hoechst with the coverslip facing upwards and adjust with forceps if necessary.
Leave the coverslips to dry for 20–30 minutes.
Gently seal the edge of each coverslip with clear nail varnish topcoat, ensuring minimal varnish on top of the coverslip.
Let the nail varnish dry for 15–20 minutes before handling further.
Seed cells onto PLO-Laminin coated 13 mm coverslips and allow them to expand for 3 days with supplemented expansion media.
Replace expansion media with differentiation base media supplemented with BDNF and FBS.

Note: The provided text includes instructions that are not directly translatable into experimental steps due to their nature (e.g., notes about mounting media, freezing-thawing protocols, SEM preparation, tables for specific conditions). These were excluded from the output as per guidelines.
Use immediately after preparation.
Do not store except for warming, which may impact stability.
Keep cells on differentiation media for a minimum of 15 days.
Change the media every 3 days during differentiation.
Proceed from step 79.
Optimize differentiation protocols for each neurogenic niche and desired cell type outcome.
